messages:
alice (infra): Heads-up: we're scheduling a preemptive security patch for the serving fleet next Thu 03:00-04:00 UTC. Goal: kernel/hypervisor patches that require rolling reboots of non-stateful nodes. No DB or storage changes.
alice (infra): This will affect a subset of hosted inference nodes (stateless GPU workers). We expect transient connection drops and a small increase in 5xxs for in-flight requests while instances restart. Estimated customer impact: brief (<30s) request errors for affected requests, overall availability target unchanged.
ben (oncall): adding this to oncall rota — I'll be primary for the window. Can someone confirm canary plan + rollback? :eyes: @frank
frank (sre): Canary plan: drain 2 instances in us-west-2 first, monitor 5xx spike and latency for 10 minutes, then continue in batches of 10. Rollback is to stop further reboots and bring back drained instances. Runbook link: <https://internal/runbooks/patching|patch-runbook>
alice (infra): exact drain command for reference:
```
# drain workertask on node
kubectl drain gpu-node-123 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=5m
# cordon
kubectl cordon gpu-node-123
```
carla (support): please post the customer-facing blurb here, we’ll use for statuspage and proactive emails. Need wording for customers on Dedicated and Hosted.
eva (product): Suggest short blurb + FAQ link. Draft below — please sanity-check.
statuspage-bot: DRAFT-TICKET created (ID: DFT-9012) for scheduled maintenance notice prep.
eva (product): Status page draft (please review):
```
Planned maintenance: rolling security patch on inference nodes
Start: Thu, 03:00 UTC
End (est): Thu, 04:00 UTC
Impact: Short, rolling restarts of some inference nodes. Customers may observe transient request errors or slightly increased latency for requests routed to restarting nodes. We do not expect data loss or long-term interruptions. If you have strict SLAs, please consider pinning to Dedicated instances or contacting support.
More info: https://status.example.com/incidents/DFT-9012
```
carla (support): LGTM. For dedicated customers we need an optional opt-out line. Also include targeted mitigation steps they can do during window.
frank (sre): Add these mitigation notes for the support KB:
- recommend clients retry on 5xx with exponential backoff (up to 3 attempts)
- use pin_model to route to dedicated pools if on Dedicated tier
- for streaming sessions, reconnect logic must resume with conversation_id header

ben (oncall): Oncall handoff plan: I'll be watching 02:45-04:30 UTC. @frank will be backup. If Pager triggers, follow runbook steps A->B->C. If >20% 5xx across region escalate to ENG-SRE incident channel and page the infra lead.
alice (infra): Customer email copy (short):
```
Subject: Planned maintenance — brief rolling reboots of inference nodes (Thu 03:00 UTC)
Body:
Hello,
We will perform a rolling security patch on our inference fleet on Thu at 03:00 UTC. This may cause brief request errors or retries for some requests. We expect the work to complete within one hour. No action is required; if you rely on strict availability, please reach out to support to discuss options.
Thanks,
Redwood Inference
```
carla (support): I'll push that to the email template queue and send to impacted Hosted customers 24h in advance. Also will queue a direct notice to Dedicated customers with opt-out instructions.
devops-bot: reminder scheduled: Thu 02:00 UTC: pre-checks run, Thu 02:45 UTC: start canary, Thu 03:00 UTC: maintenance window opens.
frank (sre): Pre-check checklist (to run 2h before):
- confirm model cache priming on hot nodes
- ensure canary keys present
- confirm autoscaling cooldowns set to 10m
- snapshot metrics dashboards

eva (product): Who will publish the statuspage update at window start? I can post the public message unless someone else prefers to own.
ben (oncall): I’ll post the statuspage at 03:00 UTC and update at completion. Format: short impact + link to support KB.
alice (infra): If things go sideways (unexpected mass 5xxs), escalation path: page infra-lead, redeploy fallback model variant that is less memory-hungry, mount additional warm nodes from spare pool. Frank will lead that.
frank (sre): noted. I'll prepare a one-click rollback playbook (stop reboots + revert new kernel) and confirm with infra-lead before executing.
carla (support): After maintenance: send completion notice to customers with summary + any action items. Draft completion blurb:
```
Maintenance complete: Rolling security patch finished at 03:42 UTC. We observed brief retries in a small fraction of requests and no prolonged degradation. If you saw errors beyond 04:00 UTC, please reply to this message and we’ll investigate.
```
eva (product): Also propose an internal postmortem template to capture lessons if we exceed thresholds. Short template below — please add items:
```
- Summary of event
- Timeline (key actions)
- Customer impact (est % of requests affected, duration)
- Root cause / contributing factors
- Mitigations and follow-ups
- Owner for each follow-up
```
ben (oncall): all set from my side. tagging the cloud-network team for FYI. @cloud-net
alice (infra): Thanks all. Action items: carla to schedule outbound comms, ben to own statuspage, frank to prepare rollback. We'll reconvene in #eng-oncall 45m before start for final go/no-go. :calendar: 
statuspage-bot: Scheduled maintenance placeholder created: https://status.example.com/incidents/DFT-9012 (public announcement pending)
carla (support): ack — sending 24h notice now, will paste the sent copy below when done.
ben (oncall): quick note — add a Slack pinned message in #incidents with the runbook link and contact list during the window.
alice (infra): pinned message done. Good luck, team. :shipit:
